GET STARTED / WINDOWS

Install the Python MCP bridge.

Keep OpenMausBot running. Your MCP client will launch the bridge when it needs it.

1. Check the requirements

  • Windows, Python 3.10+ and Node.js available on PATH.
  • An installed and running OpenMausBot app.
  • For ChatGPT: custom MCP plugin access and an authorized Secure MCP Tunnel.

The verified environment used Python 3.14.7. The dependency lock records the exact tested versions.

2. Clone and set up

git clone https://github.com/n1s1th/openmausbot-python-bridge.git
cd openmausbot-python-bridge
.\setup.ps1
.\verify.ps1
.\verify.ps1 -Live

The default verification runs portable unit tests. -Live also checks the real app through stdio, including health and bot listing. It does not message or modify a live bot.

3. Configure your MCP client

Use the example client configuration. Replace both placeholder paths with the absolute paths on your computer. Point the command to .venv/Scripts/python.exe and its argument to bridge.py.

4. Verify a real tool call

Call OpenMausBot's get_system_health tool, then list_bots. Show the actual tool results.

Expect status: connected and app: openmausbot, followed by your real bot list. A text-only assertion is not proof.

Configuration

VariablePurpose
OPENMAUSBOT_MCP_SCRIPTOverride the installed vendor mcp-server.js path.
OPENMAUSBOT_URLExplicit loopback HTTP origin. Default: http://127.0.0.1:8799.
OPENMAUSBOT_TOKENOptional paired session token required by upstream for some actions.

The default script is under %LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs/openmausbot/resources/server/mcp-server.js. Set overrides in the launching process environment. The bridge does not automatically load .env files.

PowerShell scripts blocked?

Use Python directly without changing machine execution policy:

python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-lock.txt
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q -m "not live"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe bridge.py

When launched manually, the stdio server waits for a client; an idle terminal is normal. Press Ctrl+C to stop it.
